---
title: "Code owners for sensitive paths"
description: "Which paths need the security reviewer's approval, and how that interacts with agent-authored pull requests."
---

The `main` ruleset requires code-owner review. `.github/CODEOWNERS` assigns the
security reviewer (`@vhpx`) to the paths where a mistake has the widest blast
radius:

- CI, workflows and repository automation (`.github/`, `scripts/ci/`)
- authentication, sessions, SSO and request guards (`packages/auth`,
  `packages/sso`, `packages/turnstile`, `packages/supabase`, the satellite session
  validator, web's auth and SSO API routes, every app's `proxy.ts`, and the API
  proxy guard and required-MFA runtime in `packages/utils`)
- scheduled job routes authenticated by the cron secret (`apps/*/src/app/api/cron/`)
- database migrations and RLS (`apps/database/supabase/migrations/`)
- code-execution infrastructure (`apps/devbox-control`, `packages/devbox`)
- payments (`packages/payment`, `packages/payment-core`, and the payment API and
  webhooks in `apps/pay`)
- `CODEOWNERS` itself

Paths not listed have no code owner and follow the normal review rules. Importing an
owned package does not protect its callers, so list the calling routes and guards
themselves when they make security decisions.

## Agent-authored pull requests

GitHub never counts an author's own approval. Agent pull requests are currently
opened with the security reviewer's account, so a change to an owned path cannot
collect a code-owner approval until agents author pull requests as the
`tuturuuu-bot` GitHub App. Until then, such a pull request merges only through
an authorized administrator bypass after an independent agent security review,
and GitHub records that bypass. Once `tuturuuu-bot` authors agent pull requests,
the reviewer's approval satisfies the rule normally.

## Changing ownership

Adding or removing an owned path is itself an owned change. Keep the list to
security-sensitive code; owning broad trees slows every pull request without
adding review value.
